text:
Maria: Quick heads-up: Ruby quickstart has a bad curl header and missing require. The curl uses "Auth: Bearer" instead of "Authorization: Bearer" so newbies get 401s. Also the Ruby snippet omits the require line so direct copy/paste fails.

Maria: Current (broken) curl snippet:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Auth: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```

Devon: Oof. Which file?

Maria: docs/quickstarts/ruby/README.md around line ~42. I'll open a PR to fix header and add `require 'redwood_inference'`.

Sam: We renamed the gem earlier; confirm `require` name matches the published gem so we don't oscillate.

Priya: Can we add a tiny docs CI check that runs curl snippets against docs-staging and fails on 401 or wrong header? Might prevent regressions.

Devon: We can add a docs-snippet-lint action that parses code blocks and sanity-checks headers and env var names. Lightweight.

Maria: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/1240 — fixes header, adds `require 'redwood_inference'`, clarifies REDWOOD_API_KEY, and a CONTRIBUTING note about testing snippets.

docs-bot: Issue #3426 created for quickstart snippet mismatch (reporter: Maria).

Priya: Nice. Once CI green merge and backport to 1.0.

Maria: Merged and backported. Added follow-up ticket to standardize Ruby requires across docs.

Sam: Thanks — this avoids a bunch of onboarding friction. :thumbsup:
